title: nats.Subscription implementers must provide WaitReady
answers: How do I know a NATS subscription is actually established vs just locally queued?
Adding a new nats.Subscription implementation breaks the build
Why does my fake/mock Subscription need a WaitReady method?
body:
Symptom: a watcher believes it is receiving live events but the SUB frame was only queued locally while the client was disconnected, so events are silently missed during a snapshot-to-live handoff.
Root cause: pkg/infra/nats/subscriber.go previously returned the raw nats.go Subscription, which has no way to tell 'queued' from 'server acknowledged'.
Fix pattern: the Subscription interface (pkg/infra/nats/subscriber.go:Subscription) now requires WaitReady(ctx) in addition to Unsubscribe(); the real implementation (readySubscription.WaitReady) calls conn.FlushWithContext to force a round-trip ack. Any type implementing nats.Subscription (including test fakes) must add WaitReady.
Constraints: WaitReady's ctx must carry a deadline; ordinary subscribers that don't need handoff guarantees can ignore the result, but snapshot-to-live style consumers must call it before trusting delivery.
applies: any code implementing or consuming pkg/infra/nats.Subscription, including test fakes in pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/informer and pkg/storage/unified/informer
says: Watch events stop arriving after connection failure and recovery
Real-time subscription gets confirmed locally but not by server
How to verify live events subscription is truly established
Mock subscription implementation in tests needs additional confirmation method
Event messages get missed because subscription confirmation is incomplete
search: The nats.Subscription interface requires implementations to provide a WaitReady(ctx) method that calls conn.FlushWithContext to ensure server-acknowledged subscriptions before claiming liveness. This prevents silent event loss during snapshot-to-live handoffs where a SUB frame may be queued client-side but not yet processed by the server. The context passed to WaitReady must carry a deadline; only snapshot-to-live style consumers need to call it before trusting delivery, though ordinary subscribers can ignore the result. Any type implementing pkg/infra/nats.Subscription must provide WaitReady, including test fakes in pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/informer and pkg/storage/unified/informer. When consuming subscriptions, call sub.WaitReady(ctx) after Subscribe() to confirm server-side liveness before forwarding events.
